summary: A community feature spotlighting unsung local volunteers, including Lydia Martinez of 'Senior Smiles' and Malik Johnson of 'Youth Forward'. It argues volunteers need better support through funding, a volunteer network, encouragement and training, skill matching, and long-term sustainability planning, citing proposals from the city council and residents.
one_line: Profiles of two local volunteers and proposals for funding, networking, training, skill matching and sustainability to better support community volunteer work.
key_facts: The team has been highlighting unsung community volunteers since September 1, 2023.
Lydia Martinez, a 58-year-old retired nurse, has run 'Senior Smiles' every Monday and Thursday since October 10, 2023, delivering meals and providing companionship and care to the elderly.
Malik Johnson, 34, works at the local factory and tutors at-risk youth in the evenings through 'Youth Forward', which began November 15, 2023.
Community projects usually operate on shoe-string budgets, relying on volunteers' own pockets or unpredictable donations.
On December 27, 2023, the city council proposed a new fund dedicated exclusively to volunteer-driven projects.
On January 12, 2024, local resident James Walton suggested a central volunteer hub for exchanging experiences, ideas, and resources.
Sara Nguyen, a mother of two leading a recycling initiative since February 5, 2024, pointed out the lack of accessible project management courses for volunteers.
On March 4, 2024, local attorney David Kim proposed a program matching professionals with volunteer opportunities aligned with their expertise.
The article notes a scarcity of legal professionals in the volunteer pool despite substantial need for legal guidance in non-profits.
Sustainability encompasses volunteer retention, project scalability, and continuous community engagement, and relies on succession planning and community ownership.
Volunteers like Lydia and Malik can burn out, and projects can falter without a sustainable long-term plan.
